headline: Leavitt and Brennan lead Boston College past Penn State in wire-to-wire rout
body: Boston College's passing game was simply too much for Penn State to contain on Saturday, as Sam Leavitt carved up the defense with surgical precision en route to 408 yards and four touchdowns in a dominant 44-22 victory. Leavitt's accuracy—completing 28 of 38 attempts—kept the chains moving all afternoon, and his connection with wideout Brennan proved impossible for the Penn State secondary to disrupt. Brennan hauled in seven catches for 100 yards and two scores, establishing himself as the go-to target when Boston College needed to move the ball downfield.

Penn State's offense showed flashes, particularly through the air where Edwards amassed 135 receiving yards on ten receptions and the staff orchestrated three scoring drives. But the volume tells the story: Boston College's defense held the Nittany Lions to just 56 rushing yards, forcing them into obvious passing situations and making the job easier for the Boston College secondary. Myers managed 296 passing yards in a losing effort, but without any genuine ground game to lean on, Penn State became predictable. Boston College's defense, led by Green's steady tackling, prevented the big plays that might have kept Penn State in striking distance.

The Eagles' balanced attack—399 passing yards paired with just enough efficiency on the ground to avoid one-dimensional tendencies—gave Penn State no single weakness to exploit. This was a thorough, complete performance where Boston College controlled tempo, capitalized in the red zone, and made the kinds of plays on third and fourth down that separate contenders from pretenders.
turningPoint: Boston College's early establishment of vertical passing routes forced Penn State's defense to play with deep coverage, which opened the middle of the field and allowed Leavitt to operate with sustained drives that drained the clock and kept Penn State's offense on the sideline.

unsungHero.name: WR Edwards
unsungHero.why: Edwards was Penn State's lone bright spot in a lopsided loss, accumulating 135 yards on ten catches to keep his team moving the ball when the run game and overall offensive scheme fell apart around him.
